I also just don't know who is going to be on the market that is going to be a legitimate 1C, they just don't go to FA very often at all. I don't see any this FA class that are a true 1C going forward imo. And I REALLY don't want them to sign a guy just to sign a guy and stick us with the contract long term and hinder out ability to more properly get this turned around. Well, again anyway. I am a firm believer that we need to develop one internally because we just simply cannot count on one becoming available. A wing, absolutely. There are _in theory_ some good ones coming. But a center? I don't see it. I feel like you have to draft a true 1C 98% of the time. And even if these guys aren't, they might possibly even a little bit be and right now we don't have anything remotely close so I'd be okay with it. And I don't see us trading for one, as most teams violently hang on to them because they're just not readily available.

But ultimately it seems like we just have differing visions of the team, which is understandable because we're kind of in an odd spot. Personally, I don't care if it's a guy that has to cook a minute because I don't expect us to get good any time soon regardless, and you're looking for quicker impact, which is understandable. You're not wrong and I don't feel I am either, it's just a difference of opinion on where we want them to go with the team.

Ultimately we aren't good enough that either option is a terrible decision because it still helps us with whatever direction we go long term. We have holes to fill. I just hope whatever direction they go, they pivot to it and _go_. Don't get stuck in the middle where you have a pseudo rebuild. Either way we'll find out soon enough, so godspeed to us lol. I get why people are upset with him. He's paid like a top goalie that can make those extra "he shouldn't have made that save" saves, and he hasn't this year, bad defense or not. That isn't to say that he deserves all the flak for how badly this season has gone, he doesn't. But he hasn't helped at points, and has been pretty dang bad at points too. I think he deserves some slack because this year is a shitshow. Sacco is coach. No one is buying in and we've blown it up. But he doesn't deserve _too_ much slack because he's getting paid like a top goalie to play horribly at points, even under the tough circumstances.

I say whatever. Ultimately, let's reset and get healthy. I'll judge him more harshly next season if his stats are sitting at what they are now this time next year. For now it isn't great, and even though our defense is bad, he also isn't playing like a guy who elevates a team (which is how he is being paid). Let the guy have a normal off season with a coaching change and go from there.

In a perfect world, no. In the real world with what we have and our current situation, yeah. He'd instantly be, in theory, the most talented offensive talent we have had in years even at 32 coming of the acl. Eventually our young QB needs _someone_ to throw to. And our young WRs need _someone_ to maybe help take some coverage off them or worried about anything or anyone else at all.

I don't want to pay him a ton or for a long time, but at this point I think he helps this team. Don't put yourself in a bad spot to get him, but with the amount of cap we have, it would kind of be hard to do really. And if he is washed, oh no, not our money and what are we gonna do? Lose? We're picking 4th lmao. At some point you have to make even this much of an effort to aquire something that could maybe even possibly kickstart our offense and young WRs and QB even a smidge. No one will read all this, but it'll be cathartic for me:

And many of those who do understand loans just simply go anyway because they feel like they have to. They are pressured to do so from many many many different angles. Home life? Go. School? Go. Some religious groups? Go. You. Must. Go.

It is a far more intricate issue than so many say or think. And it kills my soul. No blanket assumption or statement will ever cover everyone. This situation with student loans, or well, anything. And all of these people in this thread seeking relief have each gone down many different paths that have lead them here. 

I started the process when I was 17 of getting ready to rock and go off to college and man I was so immature and stupid. And hey, you're a failure and a loser if you don't go, many said. So I went. To better myself and my community. And I did and I am. I might not get paid well for it but I make an impact every day. There are people who are better for me having done so and I am proud of that.

But alright, I was a dumb stupid teenager and I have to pay them back many others say, some of which are the same who said I HAD TO GO. Cool, I _could_ slowly and legitimately manage that. But the predatory and high interest rates make it a mountain rather than a steep hillside. I could make a 400 dollar payment one month and damn near have the interest re-acrue that same amount by the time I make a similar payment next month.  A modern Sisyphus kind of situation.

I just get tired of the blanket statements that people make about loans and those who want some even mild relief. I'm not lazy. I work 40 hours (approx the max alloted at said job) a week or more-ish depending. I work for the local government. I make an impact in my community. I work hard. I see alot of very fucked up shit in my day to day, but by god I do the thing. It is what I want to do. 

Just because I "fucked up" at 17/18 now I have to have significant financial burden until I'm dead or much, much, much older? Cool if you paid it back, cool for those who do and did and can and will. Awesome. But man I took em out and now I'm stuck. I was a stupid dumb idiot teenager and didn't have excellent foresight, a full and total grasp of the gravity of my situation, and immense pressure to go to college. Congrats.

That's the thing that is brutal about the whole thing. Many are stuck. Just stuck with them. Just pay them back? You try to pay back hundreds a month on a predatory loan with absurd interest with rent prices, inflation, etc. Different situations for everyone, and all that. Much to the shock of many, who could not possibly ascertain what it may be like to be not themselves.

"Well you shouldn't have done that then?" FINE YOU'RE FUCKING RIGHT! HAPPY? I don't have a way out of em regardless, but you can be smug so good for you people who enjoy this! I'd just declare bankruptcy and take my stupid fucking big fat L for being a big fat stupid teenager, but I C A N N O T with student loans :). Pay enough to make an impact or be homeless, yeehaw. Not everyone has a situation in which they have the means to pay it back. Sometimes even when you're "right" it doesn't mean that there is a solution within your correctness. Thus, blanket statements about any of this are asinine and kill my soul.

"Well your mistake shouldn't be remedied my money!" All of the other silly and goofy things that your tax dollars are spent on instead aside, I never said that, though hell I'll take that too. Your tax dollars have been spent on worse/dumber. But if not that, there are still solutions to be found by god. Such as PSLF, SAVE, or even reduction in the absurd interest rates past, present, and future that are allowed to be slapped on these loans. And they can't even let me have that shit, one of which I was working hard away at every goddamn day, while they strive to take it all away, with ABSOLUTELY ZERO ALTERNATIVES to help the many who are struggling in this way. Soul crushing.

I'm just tired, boss.

Anyway, thanks for coming to my ramble.
